export_checks: 115 solver summaries in the sweep folder, 23 per level, no task twice; the 1,200 attempts cut short by Reflection's daily token limit hold no summary and are not part of the population

every run is mirror:Beam-1.0-501B-A23B at its requested level (Extra high as xhigh) on Mirror CLI 0.1.1, the install tree hash equal to the pin, a private Mirror home with only the run workspace trusted and analytics off, from bench/2026-10-23-beam-mirror-frontier-v4 with a clean source block and every task hash equal to the frozen suite lock
every integrity audit: no web, no benchmark data or answer-key paths, not contaminated
each run's token totals equal its mirror_usage receipt; no run records a cost
the population record's hash and the manifest's hash equal the ones frozen in the protocol, and every judged run's summary hash equals its manifest entry
rubric, prompts, schemas, seed, repeats, gate allowance, weights, retry rule, control hashes and both judges' pins equal the published v3.27 record

both judges passed calibration under v3.28 with no failing gate and no allowance used; no reviewer fallback; every operator marker accounted for: twelve no_source_change pairs, the two input_over_judge_limit runs and Muse's unrecoverable hedgecore review; three transport retries; 24 GPT-6.1 Sol answer-key matches recovered under recover_one_based_indexes

per-row Code quality and both combined scores recomputed and matched to the frozen summary, with intent recovery redistributed where no quirk family passed; each level's means and standard errors, per-judge means included, matched to the summary's groups

combined score, its standard error, Code quality, tasks passed and minutes per level matched to the harness card table; the card is byte-identical to the harness copy and its record names this summary
the sweep's overlap logger recorded no other benchmark job; no dashes or host paths in exported text
limits: Reflection Beam is judged by Muse Spark 1.3 and GPT-6.1 Sol, the pair v3.27 used for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, not by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 like most Frontier v4 columns (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra included): Grok 4.6's Cursor account was out of usage. Scores from different panels are not calibrated against each other.
GPT-6.1 Sol rates Beam's reviewed Code quality 10.1 to 17.6 points above Muse Spark 1.3. The published score is their mean; combined_single_judge gives each judge alone.
GPT-6.1 Sol judged these runs and is also a compared model on the card and the board; its own column comes from its own round, judged by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6.

16 runs are not judged: 15 left no code to review (three empty patches, twelve that changed no source file) and count as failed tasks; Max hedgecore passed every hidden test but its evidence could not be reviewed by either judge. The combined score is over the judged runs (11, 20, 23, 23 and 22 from Low to Max); combined_no_code_zero counts the 15 as 0 (18.90 at Low, 38.95 at Medium). Max payrollcore is published from Muse Spark 1.3 alone.
Reflection publishes no Beam price, so no cost is reported.
Model identity is harness-recorded: Mirror's conversation database names the requested model on every inference.
Mirror CLI 0.1.1 is an early beta, pinned by exact version and install tree hash; it cannot pin what Reflection's API serves under the model id.

Task files are staged without execute bits, as for every column; where Beam met Permission denied on the legacy binary, Mirror appended a note calling it a sandbox denial, and two Low runs ended believing the sandbox blocked the binary. The adapter archived model messages and usage but not tool calls, so how often Beam saw the note cannot be counted.

Reflection's daily API token limit stopped the sweep after 13 Max tasks on 2026-10-24; the 1,200 attempts it cut short were set aside unscored and the sweep resumed after the 00:00 UTC reset. No finished run was affected.
Frontier Code quality is the reviewed layer plus intent recovery and is never compared with Routine v1 Code quality.
One attempt per task and level, on the owner's Mac, local sandbox, flat 3-hour task bound, one task at a time.
publication_scope: Per-run scores, per-panel sub-scores, aggregates, judge protocol text, calibration verdicts and control means, integrity-audit verdicts, raw tokens, model calls and failed requests.
withheld: quirk answer keys (they describe hidden-test behaviour)
reviewer session identifiers and usage receipts
Mirror conversation databases and solver traces
the 1,200 attempts cut short by the daily token limit
integrity_limit: Hash checks bind the export to frozen files; they do not prove that judges were unbiased or that no training overlap exists.
